post.summary: Stores reader events of the site's own statistics. No sign-in; sent only with the visitor's consent.
post.description: Events: ArticleView, OpinionShown, OpinionSwitched, Search, ScrollDepth, InternalLinkClick, WebVitalLcp, WebVitalInp, WebVitalCls, 1 to 50 per request (analytics_events_required, analytics_too_many_events). Nothing about the sender is stored: no account, address or browser; the time is the server's. A request from a bot (by its User-Agent, read but not stored) keeps none of its events; an article view, a paragraph's opinion shown, a scroll depth or a Web Vital sent again in the same page view, and a visitor's view of an article viewed less than 30 minutes ago, are dropped. An event without a field its type needs, about an article that is not Published or about an opinion of another paragraph is dropped, and the answer says how many were kept. 429 with Retry-After: too_many_requests (this client sent too many requests).

get.summary: The whole site's own statistics over the last days, for the admin dashboard.
get.description: Read from the daily summaries, rebuilt every hour: today is counted so far. The period: days (30 by default, kept within 1 to 365) ending today (UTC), or from and to (yyyy-MM-dd, both included; to missing or later than today is today, from missing is days before to; 400 analytics_period_invalid when from is after to, analytics_period_too_long beyond 365 days). daily has every day, oldest first, zeros when nothing happened. visitors and readers summed over several days are visitor-days (the anonymous visitor id changes every UTC day). topArticles: the ten most viewed articles (title and slug null when deleted); schools: article views by the mazhab the reader had chosen, viewsWithoutSchool the rest. Traffic sources and devices are in Yandex Metrika, not here. previous: the totals of as many days just before the period, to compare with.

get.summary: What readers searched for with the site's search over the last days, and what found nothing.
get.description: Read from the daily summaries, rebuilt every hour: today is counted so far. The period: days (30 by default, kept within 1 to 365) ending today (UTC), or from and to (yyyy-MM-dd, both included; to missing or later than today is today, from missing is days before to; 400 analytics_period_invalid when from is after to, analytics_period_too_long beyond 365 days). Queries are in lower case and counted for a day only when at least minSearchers distinct visitors made them that day (a phrase one person typed is never shown, nor kept once the day is final); totals count every search. topQueries: the twenty most searched; queriesWithoutResults: the twenty that most often found no article. searchers summed over several days are searcher-days. Search phrases from external search engines are in Yandex Metrika, not here. previous: the totals of as many days just before the period, to compare with.

get.summary: What to write, finish or refresh next: unread articles, stubs with readers, blocks missing a mazhab, out-of-date articles.
get.description: Views are read from the daily summaries, rebuilt every hour: today is counted so far. The period: days (30 by default, kept within 1 to 365) ending today (UTC), or from and to (yyyy-MM-dd, both included; to missing or later than today is today, from missing is days before to; 400 analytics_period_invalid when from is after to, analytics_period_too_long beyond 365 days). The articles are taken as they are now: Published only, every language. articlesWithoutViews: articles with content, Published before the period began, not viewed in it, oldest publication first. stubsWithTraffic: stubs (no text, infobox or summary) viewed in the period, most views first. uncoveredBlocks: blocks of two or more opinions with no opinion linked to one or more canonical mazhabs (their readers get the default opinion), most views by those mazhabs' readers first. staleArticles: articles with content not saved for staleAfterDays days, most views first. Each list holds at most 50 entries; total counts them all. readers are reader-days.

get.summary: The signed-in author's statistics over the last days: only the articles they write or co-write.
get.description: Read from the daily summaries, rebuilt every hour: today is counted so far. The period: days (30 by default, kept within 1 to 365) ending today (UTC), or from and to (yyyy-MM-dd, both included; to missing or later than today is today, from missing is days before to; 400 analytics_period_invalid when from is after to, analytics_period_too_long beyond 365 days). daily has every day, oldest first: views of the user's articles and the readers who viewed any of them, as counted on that day's authorship. readers summed over several days are reader-days (the anonymous visitor id changes every UTC day). topArticles (at most ten), depth, schools and viewsWithoutSchool cover only the articles the user writes or co-writes now; depth counts the views that reached 25, 50, 75 and 100 % of the text. An admin gets their own articles here too; the whole site is /analytics/site. previous: the totals of as many days just before the period, to compare with.

get.summary: One article's statistics over the last days: views, readers, read depth, mazhabs, opinion switches, link clicks.
get.description: For an admin, or the article's own author or co-author (as for the article's history): another author gets 403 forbidden for a Published article and 404 article_not_found for one they may not see, as does an article that does not exist. Read from the daily summaries, rebuilt every hour: today is counted so far. The period: days (30 by default, kept within 1 to 365) ending today (UTC), or from and to (yyyy-MM-dd, both included; to missing or later than today is today, from missing is days before to; 400 analytics_period_invalid when from is after to, analytics_period_too_long beyond 365 days). daily has every day, oldest first, zeros when nothing happened. readers summed over several days are reader-days (the anonymous visitor id changes every UTC day). depth counts the views that reached 25, 50, 75 and 100 % of the text; schools: views by the mazhab the reader had chosen, viewsWithoutSchool the rest; internalLinkClicks: links followed from the article to another page of the site. previous: the totals of as many days just before the period, to compare with.
An article the caller may not read answers 404 article_not_found, or 410 article_gone when it was published and is now Archived.

put.summary: Saves the article's content as a new revision.
put.description: Admins may save any article, authors only those they wrote or co-author (403 forbidden for a Published article of someone else, 404 article_not_found for their other drafts). A save of a Published article is live at once; review of such edits is D4 (#20).

get.summary: Article content by slug; an old slug redirects (302) to the current one.
get.description: A current slug returns the content. A slug the article used before answers 302 Found with Location set to the current slug's URL, so clients that follow redirects get the content and can compare its slug with the one they asked for. The redirect is temporary on purpose: an old slug can become current again, and a cached permanent redirect would then loop. An article that is not Published answers 404 except to an admin or its own author or co-author. A slug, current or old, of an article that was published and then deleted or archived answers 410 article_gone, unless another article has taken it since. Slugs are unique per language: the optional locale query parameter (default ru) picks the language, and an unsupported one answers 400 locale_unsupported.

get.summary: The article's revisions, newest first.
One revision with its snapshot.
Two revisions with their snapshots; the client renders the difference.

post.summary: Rolls the article back to a revision by saving it as a new revision.
post.description: The working copy is replaced with the revision's snapshot and a new revision is written; no revision is changed or deleted. Answers 400 when the snapshot no longer fits, e.g. its slug now belongs to another article or a related article was deleted.

get.summary: The caller's autosaved draft of the article; 204 when there is none.
get.description: Each user has their own draft per article and one for a new article; it is not a revision and readers never see it. A content save (POST /articles/content, PUT /articles/{id}/content, a rollback) deletes the saving user's draft. A draft not written for 30 days is deleted.

put.summary: Writes the caller's autosaved draft of the article.
put.description: Each user has their own draft per article and one for a new article; it is not a revision and readers never see it. A content save (POST /articles/content, PUT /articles/{id}/content, a rollback) deletes the saving user's draft. A draft not written for 30 days is deleted. Errors: article_draft_snapshot_invalid, article_draft_too_large.

delete.summary: Deletes the caller's autosaved draft of the article; 204 also when there was none.

get.summary: The caller's autosaved draft of a new article; 204 when there is none.
get.description: Each user has their own draft per article and one for a new article; it is not a revision and readers never see it. A content save (POST /articles/content, PUT /articles/{id}/content, a rollback) deletes the saving user's draft. A draft not written for 30 days is deleted.

put.summary: Writes the caller's autosaved draft of a new article; baseUpdatedAt is ignored.
put.description: Each user has their own draft per article and one for a new article; it is not a revision and readers never see it. A content save (POST /articles/content, PUT /articles/{id}/content, a rollback) deletes the saving user's draft. A draft not written for 30 days is deleted. Errors: article_draft_snapshot_invalid, article_draft_too_large.

delete.summary: Deletes the caller's autosaved draft of a new article; 204 also when there was none.

post.summary: Creates an empty article (a section of the tree) with a title and a parent.
post.description: The title is trimmed; an empty one answers 400 article_title_required. The article is a Draft, placed last under the parent, with a slug made from the title.

get.summary: One page of the admin article list, filtered and sorted.
get.description: Lists the articles the caller may see (an author: Published ones plus their own), without their content. search matches the title or slug case-insensitively; status, authorId, tag (one whole tag) and locale filter exactly; mine=true keeps only the articles the caller writes or co-writes. Each item gives lastStatusChange (the latest move and its comment) when the caller may edit the article. sort is UpdatedAt (default), CreatedAt, PublishedAt (never-published last), Title or Status (workflow order); dir is Desc (default) or Asc; enum values are case-sensitive names. page is 1-based; pageSize defaults to 20 and is kept within 1 to 100.

get.summary: Article counts for the admin dashboard.
get.description: Counts the articles the caller may see (an author: Published ones plus their own): the total, those with content (an opinion, an infobox or a summary, the rule of hasContent) and without, and the number in each status. Counted in the database; no article content is loaded.

post.summary: Moves several articles to one status, each checked like a single move.
post.description: Applies POST /articles/{id}/status to each id in turn and saves each move on its own, so some may succeed while others fail. Each result carries ok, or the error code the single move would answer: article_not_found, forbidden or article_status_transition_invalid. More than 100 distinct ids answers 400 article_bulk_too_many.

get.description: Every article search engines are pointed at: Published, not noindex, and not under a non-Published parent. The same list for every caller; no content.

get.summary: The newest and the most recently updated articles, for the home page.
get.description: Two lists of articles a reader can open: Published, not under a non-Published parent, and not empty stubs. new is ordered by publishedAt, updated holds the articles saved after they were published, ordered by updatedAt; both latest first. The same lists for every caller; no content. locale defaults to ru (an unsupported one answers 400 locale_unsupported); limit is the size of each list, 6 by default, kept within 1 to 20.

get.summary: The most viewed articles of the last 30 days, for the home page.
get.description: Articles a reader can open (Published, not under a non-Published parent, not empty stubs) with the most views over the last 30 UTC days, today included, counted from the daily analytics summaries; an article with no view is not listed. No view counts and no content; the same list for every caller. locale defaults to ru (an unsupported one answers 400 locale_unsupported); limit is the size of the list, 6 by default, kept within 1 to 20.

put.summary: Renames an article and sets its parent.
put.description: Sets the title (trimmed; an empty one answers 400 article_title_required) and the parent: send the current parent to only rename. A changed parent is checked like POST /articles/{id}/move (article_parent_not_found, article_move_cycle) and places the article last under it. The slug is kept; no revision is written, UpdatedAt is set.

delete.summary: Moves the article to the trash.
delete.description: The article disappears from the site, the tree, search and every list; its slug stays reserved and its content, revisions, drafts and files are kept. If it had been published, reading it by slug answers 410 article_gone. Answers 400 article_has_children while it has children outside the trash, 404 article_not_found when there is no such article outside the trash.

post.summary: Moves an article to another status.
post.description: Allowed: Draft → InReview, InReview → Published, InReview → Draft, Published → Archived, Archived → Draft. Any other move answers 400 article_status_transition_invalid. Admins make every move; an author only Draft → InReview and InReview → Draft on an article they wrote or co-author, anything else answers 403 forbidden (404 article_not_found for someone else's draft). The optional comment (trimmed, at most 2000 characters, else 400 article_status_comment_too_long) is kept with the move in the article's status log, such as a reviewer's reason for returning the article; the answer's lastStatusChange is that move.

get.summary: The moderation queue: every article waiting for review.
get.description: Lists the InReview articles, submitted longest ago first, without content. Each gives the newest revision (what approval publishes) and the revision last published, if any, so the two can be compared through GET /articles/{id}/revisions/compare. locale filters to one language (an unsupported one answers 400 locale_unsupported); without it every language is listed. Approve or return through POST /articles/{id}/status.

post.summary: Moves an article to another parent and/or position among its siblings.
post.description: Places the article at the 0-based index among the new parent's other children (null or past the end appends) and renumbers both sibling lists. Answers 400 article_parent_not_found for an unknown parent and 400 article_move_cycle for the article itself or a descendant. Writes no revision and does not change UpdatedAt.

get.summary: The article's author and co-authors.

put.summary: Replaces the article's author and co-authors.
put.description: Duplicate co-author ids are ignored. Answers 400 user_not_found for an unknown user and 400 article_coauthor_is_author when the author is also listed as co-author.

get.summary: The trashed articles, most recently trashed first.

post.summary: Takes the article out of the trash.
post.description: It comes back with the status, slug and content it had, last among its parent's children (the root's, when the parent was purged). Answers 400 article_parent_in_trash while the parent is in the trash, 404 article_not_in_trash when the article is not there.

delete.summary: Deletes a trashed article for good.
delete.description: Removes it with its content, revisions and drafts; this cannot be undone. If it was ever published, its current and old slugs are recorded, so reading them by slug answers 410 article_gone until another article takes the slug. Its children still in the trash move to the root. Answers 404 article_not_in_trash when the article is not in the trash.

get.summary: The audit log (U-09, #135): who changed what and when, newest first. Admin only.
get.description: Logged actions: ArticleStatusChanged (publication included; fromValue/toValue are statuses), ArticleTrashed, ArticleRestored, ArticlePurged, UserRoleChanged (fromValue/toValue are roles). Filters: action, actorId, articleId, targetUserId. page from 1, pageSize 1 to 100 (50 by default). Each entry is written in the same save as its action and is never changed or removed. Only the acting user's id and the ids of the article or user acted on are kept, with the article's title at the time; no IP address, no User-Agent.

post.summary: Registers the first user as admin, then anyone with an invite, who gets the invite's role.
post.description: Sets the refresh-token cookie as well. Once a user exists an invite token is required; it is single-use. Answers 400 invite_not_found, invite_expired, invite_used or invite_revoked when it cannot be used. The password must be 12 to 128 characters (Unicode code points), not the email and not one character repeated: 400 password_too_short, password_too_long or password_too_simple otherwise. Login does not apply these rules.
Sets the refresh-token cookie as well.

post.summary: Exchanges the refresh-token cookie for a new access token.
post.description: Rotates the refresh token: the cookie is replaced, and the old token stops working. Presenting a token that was already rotated ends that device session. Requires the X-Requested-With header.

post.summary: Ends the session of the refresh-token cookie and clears the cookie.
post.description: Access tokens of that session stop working too. Requires the X-Requested-With header.

post.summary: Ends every session of the signed-in user, on every device.
post.description: Every refresh token and every access token of the user stops working, this one included.

get.summary: The signed-in user's devices: one live session each, most recently active first.

delete.summary: Ends one of the signed-in user's sessions.
delete.description: Its refresh token and access tokens stop working at once.

get.summary: The signed-in user and their current role.
get.description: The role is read from the database, so it reflects a change made after the token was issued.

post.summary: Accepts a visitor's message: an article error, a site problem or an idea. No sign-in.
post.description: The message is stored and answered with 202 at once; an issue in the project's public GitHub repository is created in the background and retried while GitHub is unavailable, so the answer does not depend on GitHub. The contact is kept only in the site's database and is never published. Errors: feedback_type_invalid, feedback_text_required, feedback_text_too_long, feedback_contact_too_long, feedback_page_url_invalid. 429 with Retry-After: too_many_requests (this client sent too many messages), feedback_limit_reached (too many messages from all visitors in the last hour). The website field is a trap for bots and must stay empty.

get.summary: Every invite, newest first, with its status. Never carries a token.

post.summary: Creates a single-use invite for a role. The token is in this response only; the server keeps its hash.
post.description: Answers 400 role_invalid, invite_lifetime_invalid or invite_note_too_long.

post.summary: Revokes an unused invite; revoking it again changes nothing.
post.description: Answers 400 invite_used when someone already registered with it, 404 invite_not_found.

get.description: Anonymous readers get only Published articles; a Published article under a non-Published parent is hidden with its subtree. Admins get every article with its status.

post.summary: Takes a browser error report from the site's own script (X-05). No sign-in.
post.description: The report is cleaned (no e-mail addresses, no query strings, no tokens) and written to the server log; nothing is stored and no address or User-Agent is kept. Always 202 for a readable body, also when the report is dropped by the overall cap. 429 with Retry-After: too_many_requests.

get.summary: The public profile of an author, by slug.
get.description: Only what readers may see: no email, no user id. Answers 404 author_not_found unless the user has a display name and is the author or a co-author of at least one Published article, so accounts cannot be listed through it. degree and institution are self-declared and given only for a user whose role is Scholar.

get.summary: The articles an author wrote or co-authored, for the author's public page.
get.description: Only articles a reader can open: Published, not under a non-Published parent, and not empty stubs; ordered by publishedAt, latest first. The same list for every caller; no content. The list may be empty for a public author. locale defaults to ru (an unsupported one answers 400 locale_unsupported); page starts at 1; pageSize is 20 by default, kept within 1 to 50. Answers 404 author_not_found exactly when GET /authors/{slug} does.

get.summary: The signed-in user's profile.
get.description: Every field is empty until the user fills it in. isPublic says whether readers can open the profile now.

put.summary: Replaces the signed-in user's whole profile.
put.description: A blank value clears its field. A blank slug keeps the current one or, the first time a display name is set, is derived from the name; clearing the name clears the slug. A changed slug is not kept as a redirect. Answers 400 with a profile_* code: profile_display_name_invalid, profile_display_name_required (a slug without a name), profile_slug_invalid, profile_slug_taken, profile_avatar_url_invalid, profile_bio_too_long, profile_degree_too_long, profile_institution_too_long, profile_links_too_many, profile_link_label_invalid, profile_link_url_invalid.

get.summary: The signed-in user's activity by week: edits and publications.
get.description: Weeks run Monday to Sunday in UTC, oldest first; the last is the current week so far, and every week is present even when empty. edits = revisions the user saved (restores included); publications = the user's articles, written or co-authored, first published that week. weeks is 12 by default, kept within 1 to 52. Only the user's own activity: it is not shown to readers.

get.summary: The four canonical schools, named in one language (I-07, #111).
get.description: locale defaults to ru (an unsupported one answers 400 locale_unsupported). name and shortName are the school's names in that language, or the Russian ones when the school has no translation into it; id and slug are the same in every language.

get.summary: Custom schools of one article.
get.description: An article that is not Published answers 404 article_not_found except to an admin or its own author or co-author, as the other article reads do; so does an article that does not exist.

post.summary: Creates a custom school for one article: admins for any article, authors for their own.

delete.summary: Deletes a custom school: admins any, authors those of their own articles.

get.summary: Full-text search over articles.
get.description: Searches the title, summary, tags and opinion texts with Russian morphology; an article matches when it holds every word of q. Only articles a reader can open are searched: Published and not under a non-Published parent. The same results for every caller, best match first. Matched words come as separate text runs (match: true), never as markup. q is trimmed and must be 2 to 200 characters (400 search_query_too_short / search_query_too_long); locale defaults to ru (an unsupported one answers 400 locale_unsupported); page starts at 1 and is kept within 1 to 100; pageSize is 10 by default, kept within 1 to 50.

get.summary: The site's IndexNow key, for the key file search engines check (/indexnow-key.txt).
get.description: The key is public by design: search engines read it from the site to trust the URLs it sends them when an article is published or unpublished. 404 indexnow_not_configured while IndexNow is off (IndexNow:Key and IndexNow:SiteUrl not both set, or IndexNow:Enabled false).

get.summary: The directory of sources, for the picker in the article editor.
get.description: Entries whose title or author contains q (case-insensitive; no q lists the directory from the start), optionally of one kind, ordered by title. limit is 20 by default, kept within 1 to 50. Readers do not need it: the content of an article carries the sources it cites.

post.summary: Adds an entry to the directory of sources.
post.description: An entry of the same kind with the same title and author (ignoring case) fails with source_duplicate, whose params.id names the existing one.

put.summary: Replaces a directory entry (admins only: it changes every article that cites it).
put.description: Saved revisions keep the source as it was when they were written.

delete.summary: Deletes a directory entry that no opinion cites (admins only).
delete.description: A cited entry fails with source_in_use (params.count citations): remove the citations first.

get.summary: Every tag with the number of articles carrying it, for the admin (M-06, #70).
get.description: Ordered by language, then name. locale, when given, lists one language (an unsupported one answers 400 locale_unsupported). articleCount counts articles of any status; a tag no article carries any more has 0.

get.summary: A tag and the articles carrying it, for the tag page.
get.description: Only articles a reader can open: Published, not under a non-Published parent, and not empty stubs; ordered by publishedAt, latest first. The same answer for every caller. Answers 404 tag_not_found when the language has no tag with this slug or no such article carries it. locale defaults to ru (an unsupported one answers 400 locale_unsupported); page starts at 1; pageSize is 20 by default, kept within 1 to 50.

put.summary: Renames a tag on every article carrying it (admins only).
put.description: A bad name answers 400 tag_name_required, tag_name_too_long (params.maxLength) or tag_name_invalid (a comma or control characters). A name another tag of the language has (ignoring case, ё as е) answers 400 tag_name_taken with params.id: merge the two instead. slug null or blank keeps the current one; a new one must be valid (tag_slug_invalid) and free in the language (tag_slug_taken). The old slug is not kept. No revision is written and updatedAt does not change.

post.summary: Merges a tag into another and deletes it (admins only).
post.description: Every article carrying the tag carries intoTagId instead, at the same place; the answer is the remaining tag. Fails with 400 tag_merge_into_itself or tag_merge_locale_mismatch, 404 tag_not_found for either tag. No revision is written and updatedAt does not change.

get.summary: A stored file, by name.
get.description: Public. Served with its own content type (only images are stored), nosniff and a year-long immutable cache. Answers 404 file_not_found.

post.summary: Uploads an avatar image; any signed-in user.
post.description: At most 512 px on the longer side. The profile is not changed: save the returned url as avatarUrl. The file goes as the multipart form field file. The format is read from the file itself, not from its name or Content-Type: only JPEG, PNG and WebP; the image is turned upright, scaled down and re-encoded as WebP without any metadata. Answers 400 with upload_file_required, upload_too_large (params.maxMegabytes), upload_type_unsupported, upload_image_invalid or upload_image_too_many_pixels (params.maxMegapixels); 429 too_many_requests past the per-user upload limit.

post.summary: Uploads an image for an article; authors and admins.
post.description: At most 2048 px on the longer side. The file goes as the multipart form field file. The format is read from the file itself, not from its name or Content-Type: only JPEG, PNG and WebP; the image is turned upright, scaled down and re-encoded as WebP without any metadata. Answers 400 with upload_file_required, upload_too_large (params.maxMegabytes), upload_type_unsupported, upload_image_invalid or upload_image_too_many_pixels (params.maxMegapixels); 429 too_many_requests past the per-user upload limit.

get.summary: Every user with their role, for choosing article authors and managing roles. Admin only: it lists emails.

put.summary: Gives a user another role; it applies from their next request.
put.description: Answers 400 last_admin_demotion when the user is the last admin, 404 user_not_found for an unknown user.

get.summary: Any user's profile, for an admin.

put.summary: Replaces any user's whole profile, for an admin.
put.description: The same rules as PUT /profile. Answers 400 with a profile_* code: profile_display_name_invalid, profile_display_name_required (a slug without a name), profile_slug_invalid, profile_slug_taken, profile_avatar_url_invalid, profile_bio_too_long, profile_degree_too_long, profile_institution_too_long, profile_links_too_many, profile_link_label_invalid, profile_link_url_invalid. Answers 404 user_not_found for an unknown user.
